title: Tequila Explained
description: Tequila has deep cultural roots, complex production and a wide range of styles. Learn its story from ancient origins to modern cocktails, and how to drink, mix and appreciate it, with expert-led videos and quizzes.
topics: The history of tequila, from pulque to premium
How tequila is made, from agave to distillation
Styles: Blanco, Reposado, Añejo, Extra Añejo and Mixto
How to drink tequila: neat, with food and in cocktails

lessons.title: Welcome to Tequila Explained
lessons.review:
Tequila is a Mexican spirit made from the blue Weber agave plant (Agave tequilana). It has a protected designation of origin, much like Champagne or Scotch.

It can only be made in the state of Jalisco and in parts of Guanajuato, Michoacán, Nayarit and Tamaulipas.

This course covers tequila's history, how it is made, the rules, and every style from blanco to añejo.

lessons.title: The history of tequila
lessons.review:
Long before tequila, the Aztecs drank pulque, a fermented (not distilled) agave drink.

Spanish settlers brought distillation in the 1500s and began distilling agave around the town of Tequila in Jalisco.

Jose Cuervo received one of the first licences to produce in 1795, and Mexico protected the name "tequila" in 1974.

questions.explain: Pulque is fermented agave sap.
Spanish settlers introduced distilling.

lessons.title: How tequila is made
lessons.review:
Agave takes around six to eight years to mature. Jimadores harvest it by hand, trimming the leaves to reveal the heart, or piña.

The piñas are cooked, traditionally in stone or brick ovens (hornos), or in steel autoclaves, to turn their starches into fermentable sugars. They are then crushed, sometimes with a stone wheel called a tahona.

The juice is fermented and usually distilled twice. It may then be bottled straight away or rested in oak.

questions.explain: Jimadores harvest agave by hand.

questions.q: The heart of the agave is called?
questions.explain: The piña is cooked and crushed.

questions.q: How long does agave take to mature?
questions.explain: Blue agave takes many years to mature.

lessons.title: Tequila rules and regulations
lessons.review:
Tequila is regulated by Mexico's official standard (the NOM) and certified by the Tequila Regulatory Council (CRT).

There are two categories. 100% agave tequila is made only from blue agave sugars. Tequila (often called mixto) must contain at least 51% agave sugars, with other sugars making up the rest.

Every bottle carries a NOM number that identifies the distillery that made it.

questions.q: Minimum agave sugars in a mixto tequila?
questions.explain: Mixto needs at least 51% agave sugars.
NOM identifies the producing distillery.

questions.q: Which tequila uses only agave sugars?
questions.explain: 100% agave tequila uses only agave.

lessons.title: Types and styles of tequila
lessons.review:
Blanco (silver): unaged or rested up to two months. Joven (gold): usually a blend or a softened blanco.

Reposado: rested two to twelve months in oak. Añejo: aged one to three years in oak barrels of up to 600 litres.

Extra Añejo: aged more than three years, a category added in 2006. Older is not "better", just different.

lessons.title: What is blanco or silver tequila?
lessons.review:
Blanco is tequila at its purest: clear, bright and full of cooked agave, citrus and pepper.

It is bottled straight after distillation or rested in steel or oak for under two months.

Blanco is the bartender's choice for Margaritas, Palomas and other fresh, citrusy cocktails.

questions.q: Blanco is best known for tasting of?
questions.explain: Unaged tequila shows the agave.

questions.q: Blanco may be rested for up to?
questions.explain: Under two months.
Blanco shines in a Margarita.

lessons.title: Reposado tequila: how long and why
lessons.review:
"Reposado" means rested. It spends two to twelve months in oak, often ex-bourbon barrels.

That short rest softens the spirit and adds light vanilla and caramel while keeping the agave character.

It is a great bridge for whisky drinkers and works neat or in richer cocktails.

questions.explain: Reposado means rested.
Two to twelve months in oak.
Oak softens and sweetens.

lessons.title: What makes gold tequila different?
lessons.review:
Gold (joven or oro) tequila is often a mixto with permitted colouring and flavouring to look and taste aged.

A higher-quality joven can also be a blend of blanco with reposado or añejo.

Read the label: "100% agave" tells you it is made only from agave, whatever its colour.

questions.explain: Many gold tequilas are coloured mixtos.

options: A blend of blanco and aged tequila
questions.explain: Joven can blend blanco with aged tequila.

questions.q: How do you know it is only agave?
options: The words "100% agave" on the label
questions.explain: Look for 100% agave.

lessons.title: What gives añejo tequila its colour?
lessons.review:
Añejo spends one to three years in oak barrels of up to 600 litres, and most of its amber colour comes from that wood.

Expect richer notes of vanilla, toffee, dried fruit and spice, with the agave still underneath.

Serve it like a fine whisky: neat or with a single large ice cube.
